artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(K_i)_{i\ge 1}$ be a sequence of nonempty compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$ such that $0\in K_i$ for every $i$ and $\operatorname{diam}(K_i)\to 0$ as $i\to\infty$. Define the achievement set
$$S=\Bigl\{\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}x_j:\ x_j\in K_j\ \text{for all } j\ge 1\Bigr\}.$$
The condition $\operatorname{diam}(K_i)\to 0$ together with $0\in K_i$ ensures that every such series converges absolutely, so $S$ is a well-defined compact subset of $\mathbb{C}$. Let $\dim_H$ denote Hausdorff dimension.

(a) Is it true generically (for example, for a generic choice of the sequence $(K_i)$ in a suitable Baire-category sense, or under mild geometric hypotheses on the $K_i$) that
$$\dim_H(S)=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\dim_H(K_i)?$$
(b) If the equality fails in general, characterize the specific classes of sequences $(K_i)$ of compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$ for which the equality $\dim_H(S)=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\dim_H(K_i)$ does hold.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a paper that resolves this specific question about the Hausdorff dimension of achievement sets of null sequences of compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$. Related recent work (e.g., on signed null sequences and Hausdorff dimension, 2025) addresses adjacent questions on sign-sum achievement sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ but does not appear to settle the equality $\dim_H(S)=\sum_i\dim_H(K_i)$ for general complex compact sets. Status therefore appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Signed null sequences and Hausdorff dimension
status_evidence.snippet: For any null sequence (a_n) in R^d, the set of sign sequences yielding a convergent series has full Hausdorff dimension; in higher dimensions analogous statements need extra hypotheses such as d linearly independent Lévy vectors.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related work treats sign-sum variants but does not resolve the stated equality for sums over compact sets K_i⊂C.
